messages:
jess: heads up - we've been seeing intermittent gRPC streaming stalls between clipper-pod -> gpu-worker across nodes in us-east-2. streams pause ~2-6s, then resume. stack shows repeated RST_STREAM and long tokenization delays.

kai: saw that too. packet loss counters on the pod NICs look low, but tcp retransmits spike. any MTU clues?

deepa: i ran a quick tcpdump on the source node, noticed a bunch of ICMP "Fragmentation needed" from the next-hop (10.1.5.2). tracepath shows path MTU drop hitting 1420.

jess: interesting — our CNI is configured for 1450. could be an egress clamp on the egress ENI or a transit-gw rule.

omar: can someone paste the tracepath + ip route for the affected node? i want to check ECMP asymmetry.

kai: paste: `tracepath 10.2.12.21` -> shows mtu 1500 -> 1420 at hop 4.

kai: and `ip -4 route get 10.2.12.21` -> resolves via eni-abc (eni has MTU 9001 but the peer path clamps to 1420).

deepa: short investigation notes: 1) path includes a transit-gw to another AZ (we didn't expect encapsulation there), 2) iptables MASQUERADE on the egress box is doing conntrack + MTU clamp per rule from a previous workaround.

jess: that matches what i found — someone added a `--clamp-mss-to-pmtu` iptables rule ages ago to fix internet path problems. it's applying to east-west traffic now due to SNAT on kube-proxy in our config.

kai: that would cause oversized segments to be chopped, and with GSO/TSO enabled the kernel can hand off big skbs which get split later => gRPC stream reassembly timing weirdness. test idea: toggle `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off` on one node and see if stalls disappear.

omar: i also hit this in a lab once — PMTU blackhole + GSO causes packets to be chopped into fragments at egress mid-path, and some reassembly gets delayed under load. the symptom is short stalls not full disconnects.

deepa: quick mitigation advised: 1) remove the clamp rule from the egress NAT host for internal pod CIDRs, 2) set `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` cluster-wide as a bandaid, 3) schedule a rolling config change to CNI `mtu` to match the real path if encapsulation persists.
jess: i'm going to roll a patch to the NAT hosts to exclude pod cidr from the clamp rule and enable tcp_mtu_probing on a canary node. will report results.

infra-bot: deploy started: update/egress-nat/remove-clamp (canary) — CI passed, rolling to 1 node.

kai: thanks. if this clears canary, full roll should be quick. also plan follow-up: audit any other MASQ rules that may have been added during past incidents.

jess: canary looks good so far: no gRPC stalls for 30m on that node, retransmits back to baseline. Omar, want me to ping you for post-roll validation steps?

omar: yeah please. also add a short doc blurb in infra runbook about "avoid clamp for internal CIDRs" and how to troubleshoot (tracepath, ethtool, sysctl).

deepa: noted. logging the action items: 1) remove clamp for pod cidr (done canary), 2) enable tcp_mtu_probing on cluster (PR queued), 3) run perf test with long-lived gRPC streaming to verify, 4) update runbook.

jess: thanks team. marking this as resolved-if-no-regressions in 24h. :white_check_mark:
